questions.title: Social media series
questions.prompt: Read this paragraph on plastic in rivers: "Plastic thrown into drains travels to rivers and finally the sea. It breaks into tiny pieces that fish eat, and these particles can end up in the food we eat."

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Design a series of 3 square social-media posts to make young people aware of this issue.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Write a caption (max 15 words) for each post; the last should end with an action.

analysis.idealApproach: Spend 2 minutes planning: write one line per frame (problem → reaction → help → outcome). Use a wide shot to set the scene (a city road with parked cars), then move closer for the emotional moment. Show feelings through posture rather than faces, keep characters consistent, and keep captions to the point. Stop drawing at 21 minutes to add captions.

Walk through the situation hour by hour and list needs under comfort, health, safety, communication and dignity before drawing. Arrange the items in a tidy grid or 'knolling' layout so the sheet looks organised. For the redesign, solve one specific problem of THIS user (not a generic gadget) and show the user actually using it, with 2–3 labels.

Pick something you can draw convincingly from memory. Use one 3/4 view and one side view, with consistent light. In the write-up, cover form, material, use and feeling, and end with a concrete improvement. Count roughly 200 words: examiners notice when limits are ignored.

Decide the one thing people must understand in 2 seconds. Use sign conventions (red circle = prohibition, blue = information, triangle = warning), high contrast, and minimal words, ideally bilingual. The placement sketch should show the viewer's eye level and the direction they approach from: this is where most students lose marks.

List the object's properties first (shape, material, hollow, light, transparent…) and give each use a DIFFERENT property, so the three ideas don't overlap. Make each context unmistakable with one or two details (a bed for a hospital, a counter for a shop). Divide the sheet into three equal panels before you start.

Plan the series as hook → why it matters → what to do. Keep one layout, palette and type style across all three so they read as a set. Use one strong visual metaphor per post and borrow facts from the paragraph. The final post's call to action should be specific and doable.
